profileEvidence.summary: Watchful around strangers, Kars dogs traditionally protect livestock and the people tending them in northeastern Turkey. Their job is to stay with cattle, sheep or goats and deter predators and intruders, rather than move the stock. The named regional population was reported at a 1996 shepherd-dog symposium and has since been studied and bred at Kafkas University.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A watchful northeastern Turkish livestock guardian, working alongside cattle, sheep and goats to deter intruders.
profileEvidence.author: L worker B

profileEvidence.summary: Boisterous and outgoing, Tasmanian Smithfields can retain the independent approach of a farm worker. Breeder Matthew Larner describes dogs that start training later and work more naturally than more controllable herding dogs. Farmers have shaped this variable working type for moving cattle and sheep, while keeping it as a companion too.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: An outgoing Tasmanian working type, shaped by farmers for cattle and sheep and described as a natural worker.
